text: CHAPTER 22
speaker: Narrator

text: The Desert Remembers
speaker: Narrator
note: Chapter title. Leave a clean beat before story begins.

text: The first three days were almost ordinary.
speaker: Narrator

text: The desert remained what it had always been: heat that baked thought into dust, wind that found every seam in clothing, and long stretches of nothing that made a man question every choice that had brought him there. The dunes looked frozen in the act of becoming waves. Wind had carved ribs into the sand where forgotten roads once ran. Zik had crossed enough of it to know that ordinary did not mean safe. It only meant nothing had decided to kill them yet.
speaker: Narrator

text: They rode in a loose line. Balag led the donkeys, muttering the old wards his grandfather had taught him whenever the wind shifted. Enhedu rode ahead, watching the horizon the way a thief watches a locked door. Ninsun kept to the middle, writing whenever they stopped. Zik brought up the rear, the journal heavy against his ribs and the mark on his palm itching worse with every mile.
speaker: Narrator

text: On the second night, around a small fire, the friction that had been simmering since the gate finally surfaced.
speaker: Narrator

text: Ninsun spread three scraps of parchment across her knees.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: We should be documenting everything. The map, the symbol, the exact location of the first chamber, the way the writing changes. This knowledge could alter how the entire region is understood.
speaker: Ninsun

text: Zik was checking a donkey's strap.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: We document what sells. The rest is weight.
speaker: Zik

text: That is an astonishingly small way to look at the world.
speaker: Ninsun

text: It's a practical way.
speaker: Zik

text: Balag poked the fire.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: Some things should stay buried. My grandfather said the deep desert doesn't forget. It just waits for someone stupid enough to remind it.
speaker: Balag

text: Enhedu's voice came from the shadows.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: Then we remind it with a sharp knife and a heavier purse. Knowledge is a weapon. Stop treating it like a sacred relic.
speaker: Enhedu

text: Balag looked at her.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: You say that like you've ever learned anything you couldn't sell.
speaker: Balag

text: I've learned plenty of things I couldn't sell.
speaker: Enhedu

text: Name one.
speaker: Balag

text: Enhedu considered, then smiled without warmth.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: No.
speaker: Enhedu

text: Balag gave a short nod, as if the answer confirmed something he had already decided.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: Thought so.
speaker: Balag

text: The silence that followed was sharper than the argument.
speaker: Narrator

text: Ninsun shook her head.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: You are all impossible.
speaker: Ninsun

text: Zik said nothing. The argument was older than any of them; it had simply found new mouths.
speaker: Narrator

text: The third day brought the first wrong thing.
speaker: Narrator

text: They found an old well just before dusk—an ancient ring of stone half-buried in sand, the remains of a road running past it toward nowhere. Footprints led to the edge and stopped. None led away.
speaker: Narrator

text: Balag circled it twice before approaching.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: Someone's used it recently.
speaker: Balag

text: While the others examined the tracks, he crouched at the rim, took a small carved bead from a pouch at his belt, and set it carefully on the stones. No one commented. Later, when Ninsun asked why, he only said,
speaker: Narrator

text: Payment.
speaker: Balag

text: When she asked to whom, he answered,
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: Exactly.
speaker: Balag

text: Zik looked down the shaft. The darkness was deeper than the angle of the sun allowed. He lowered the bucket. The rope paid out far longer than the depth should have permitted. When the bucket finally struck water the sound that came back was wrong—hollow, delayed, almost like an answer.
speaker: Narrator

text: They drank. The water was warm, yet it tasted of iron and cold stone, as though it had never seen sunlight.
speaker: Narrator

text: That night the donkeys refused to graze. Both animals stood rigid, ears pointed toward the same empty stretch of dark. Enhedu was the first to speak.
speaker: Narrator

text: Did anyone hear that?
speaker: Enhedu

text: No one had. The donkeys had.
speaker: Narrator

text: A thin line appeared in the sand several paces beyond the firelight, moving slowly toward the camp as if something beneath the surface were dragging a finger across the desert. It stopped. The mark on Zik's palm went cold. Then the line vanished.
speaker: Narrator

text: Balag got the animals under control.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: We leave at first light.
speaker: Balag

text: No one disagreed.
speaker: Narrator

text: Zik sat apart with the journal. The page he had left blank was no longer blank. A single line had appeared in a hand that was not his father's and not quite his own:
speaker: Narrator

text: NOT YET.
speaker: Narrator
note: Written text (ledger/inscription/journal, not in Bel-iddin's hand). Cold, deliberate read.

text: He closed the book before anything else could form.
speaker: Narrator

text: Somewhere beyond the firelight the desert shifted, patient and vast, as if it had only just remembered their names.
speaker: Narrator
